rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning to the Prophet’s wives, left unnamed out of respect for him, leads to imitating his complete manners and the guardians who helped form theirs.
rows.anchor: ولما أبلغ سبحانه في عتاب أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wives’ virtues arose from their guardians’ good upbringing, perfected by the Prophet’s good companionship and their adoption of his noble character.
rows.anchor: بحسن تأديب أوليائهن لهن وإكمال ذلك الأدب بحسن عشرته صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address generalizes the prior admonition: enjoin right and forbid wrong first among those nearest, securing God’s and spouses’ rights and household harmony.
rows.anchor: دالة على وجوب الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر للأقرب فالأقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address begins with the youngest, implying older Muslims have followed the example since entering Islam and need no new order.
rows.anchor: مخاطبة لأدنى الأسنان إشارة إلى أن من فوقهم تأسى من حين دخوله في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here those who believe are those who acknowledged the faith.
rows.anchor: أي أقروا بذلك { قوا أنفسكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protect yourselves by following the Prophet’s conduct toward Creator and creation, first observing proper manners with God and then with other people.
rows.anchor: أي اجعلوا لها وقاية بالتأسي به صلى الله عليه وسلم في أدبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His example includes gentleness toward people who deserve gentleness, as an act of honoring the Creator.
rows.anchor: في لينه لمن يستحق اللين من الخلق تعظيما للخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is a shepherd responsible for the household, and family includes women, children, and everyone covered by that name.
rows.anchor: من النساء والأولاد وكل من يدخل في هذا الاسم قوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guard family from the Fire through counsel and discipline so they acquire the character of the Prophet’s household.
rows.anchor: بالنصح والتأديب ليكونوا متخلقين بأخلاق أهل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن العاص
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ transmits a Prophetic report that a father gives no gift to a child better than good manners; Aḥmad and al-Ṭabarānī are named, with no grading.
rows.anchor: كما روى أحمد والطبراني عن سعيد بن العاص رضي الله عنه رفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People and stones, the softest and hardest things, are named as fuel; anything between them is fuel all the more.
rows.anchor: { الناس والحجارة } أي ألين الأشياء وأصلبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ being over Hell signifies their authority and control over it, enabled by God’s discipline of them.
rows.anchor: دلالة على تمكنهم من التصرف فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are coarse in body and heart, stern toward those who deserve it because they disobeyed God.
rows.anchor: أي في الأبدان والقلوب فظاظة على أهلا لاستحقاقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are strong in everything they undertake, in speech and action.
rows.anchor: أي في كل شيء يحاولونه بالقول والفعل حتى روي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed report says one angel casts seventy thousand unbelievers into the Fire in a single throw; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: حتى روي أن الواحد منهم يلقي بالدفعة الواحدة في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their severity is applied to sinners according to the measure they deserve, as clarified by the declaration that they never disobey God.
rows.anchor: يوقعون غلظتهم وشدتهم بأهل المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They never disobey God at any time regarding whatever command He has given them.
rows.anchor: { لا يعصون الله } أي الملك الاعلى في وقت من الأوقات

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو وثوبات
rows.claim: The Prophet said, as transmitted by Ibn Mājah from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr and by al-Ṭayālisī from Thawbān, Be upright, though you will not attain perfection; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: فيما أخرجه ابن ماجة عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما والطيالسي عن ثوبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike humans, who may omit a pillar, condition, or time through forgetfulness or sleep, or fail in recommended acts through whispers and inner talk, angels execute every command fully.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المطيع منا قد يخل ببعض المأمور به في ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb portrays renewed, continuing performance with each command.
rows.anchor: أي مجددين مع كل أمر على سبيل الاستمرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive construction hints at how easily they obey and leaves God as the obvious, understood commander.
rows.anchor: لما لم يسم فاعله كناية عن سهولة انقايدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers addressed are those who violated proper conduct toward the Prophet, then toward God and the rest of creation.
rows.anchor: أي بالإخلال بالأدب في النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأداهم ذلك إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Prophet is foremost among those owed proper conduct, deliberately breaching manners toward him is unbelief, and this Fire is for such people.
rows.anchor: فكان تعمد الإخلال بالأدب معه كفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not labor to manufacture excuses that erase your failure: this is the day of recompense, not excuses, and the time for apologizing has passed.
rows.anchor: أي تبالغوا في إظهار العذر وهو إيساع الحيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If even elaborate pleas are forbidden because useless, ordinary excuses are forbidden a fortiori; this cuts off hope and deepens anguish.
rows.anchor: وإذا نهى عن المبالغة في الاعتذار لعدم نفعها كان النهي عن مطلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restrictive wording says that on this day they receive only recompense.
rows.anchor: { إنما تجزون } أي في هذا اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their persistent deeds are likened to an ingrained disposition; God can make each person’s recognizable deed-image the painful punishment proportionate to that person’s desert.
rows.anchor: أي على سبيل الإصرار ولا بعد على الله في أن يصور لكل إنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura follows al-Mulk’s contrast between the astray and guided and between bad and good action, then its closing image of life-giving water.
rows.anchor: في آخر ( الملك ) والمسيء والمحسن في العمل أولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mulk’s closing water points to God’s power to restore life: none but the fully powerful can bring it back, and the One who revives bodies can revive dead spirits through knowledge.
rows.anchor: فكان قادرا على كل ما يريد , وكان لا يقدر على كل ما يريده إلا من كمل علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowledge bestowed on the unlettered Prophet demonstrates the breadth of divine power and knowledge; this sura opens with the named final letter of the previous sura’s closing phrase.
rows.anchor: دل على شمول قدرته بكمال علمه بما أفاده على النبي الكريم الأمي من العلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn is an alphabet letter associated by its place in words for light, fire, growth, intelligence, purity, counsel, news, excellence, rescue, carving, and regret with manifestation and knowledge.
rows.anchor: هذه الكلمة حرف من حروف المعجم وهي اسم لمسمى به ظهور الأشياء وعلمها

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq is reported to have said every book has a secret and the Quran’s secret is these letters, known only to God; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أنه قال : لكل كتاب سر وسر القرآن هذه الحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn is shared in Arabic by the letter, inkpot, fish, and sword blade; its sukun first signals a letter but does not exclude the other senses, since Arabic can pause a word for emphasis.
rows.anchor: هذا الحرف مشتركا في اللغة بين حرف المعجم والدواة والحوت وشفرة السيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed meanings include the tablet, the correct word, and a fish; these senses allow the letter’s encompassing reference to any element.
rows.anchor: وقيل : النون اللوح , والنونة الكلمة من الصواب , والسمكة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Through ʿIkrima, Ibn ʿAbbās interprets nūn as the final letter of al-Raḥmān, the inkpot, and the cosmic fish al-Bahmūt; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه آخر حروف الرحمن والدواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath may encompass the letter and pen, signifying comprehensive knowledge, or the sword and its momentous effects; all proposed referents point to encompassing power.
rows.anchor: ويكون الإقسام وقع بالنون والقلم علوا للإحاطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever the intended sense, nūn signifies encompassing hidden realities whose results appear as decree and destiny, either misery or felicity.
rows.anchor: وكيفما كان المراد فهو الإحاطة , وهو سر باطن لا يظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn issues from a very open, easy, light articulation at the tongue tip and upper gum; nūn, lām, and rāʾ are liquid letters because edges are slippery.
rows.anchor: فغنه يخرج مما بين طرف اللسان وفويق الثنايا من اللثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among these letters, nūn has the firmest articulation where tongue and gum meet, and its name repeats its sound, ending where it began.
rows.anchor: والنون أمكنها في هذا المخرج وأشدها انطباقا فيما بين اللسان واللثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter’s frame rests on the prominent, strong wāw, itself a liquid letter; liquid letters are light on the tongue and readily combine, unlike ṣāmitah letters.
rows.anchor: واختص بكون عماده وقوامه الحرف الأقوى الأظهر ذا الرفعة والعلو وهو الواو الزلقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic words longer than three letters cannot consist only of ṣāmitah letters; at least one liquid letter must occur, while alif is outside both classes as unlocated breath.
rows.anchor: وأما المصمتة فمنعت أن تنفرد بنفسها في لغة العرب في كلمة هي أكثر من ثلاثة أحرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn’s open, light articulation and its voiced, open, low quality, between stop and fricative, with nasalization when quiescent, mirror knowledge’s breadth and penetration into hidden things.
rows.anchor: فقد ناسبت بمخرجها لسعته وخفته ووصفها بالزلاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn shares nasalization with mīm, but is the original in nasalization and manifestation, matching knowledge’s priority and prominence.
rows.anchor: ويشاركه الميم في الغنة كما أنه يشاركه في أن له حظا من الظهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a letter that may be augmentative or original, nūn parallels knowledge: it expands when cultivated and contracts when neglected.
rows.anchor: وهو أيضا من حروف الذبذبة والزيادة التي لا تستقر على حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn can replace other letters but is not itself replaced, just as knowledge is foundational rather than subordinate to other things.
rows.anchor: وهو من حروف الأبدال التي تبدل من غيرها ولا يكون غيرها بدلا منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a sound, healthy consonant rather than a weak letter, nūn reflects the strength and solidity of knowledge.
rows.anchor: وهو من الحروف الصحيحة وليست معتلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author classifies nūn as a hidden, mixed letter and among oral ṣumm letters, defined by firm, established articulation; these qualities fit knowledge.
rows.anchor: وهو إذا كان مخفي من الحروف المشربة ويقال لها المخالطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn’s point of articulation and all its attributes correspond to knowledge, establishing knowledge as the sura’s central purpose.
rows.anchor: فقد انطبقت بمخرجها وجميع صفاتها على العلم الذي هو مقصود السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen’s role in displaying and spreading knowledge and disclosing secrets is obvious to anyone with reason.
rows.anchor: وأما رتبة القلم في بيان العلم وإظهاره وكشف خفاياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn accompanies every letter through tanwīn; since vowel marks signal life, tanwīn after them signals knowledge that completes life.
rows.anchor: أنه يصحب كل حرف لأن حده هو ما يعبر عنه التنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn’s name stands for light and anything that reveals hidden things: knowledge, sun and moon, other lights, eyes, ink, and tools that make forms visible.
rows.anchor: ثم هو اسم لكل ما يظهر ما خفي باطنا كالعلم في الإدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author extends nūn’s symbolism to plant growth and guidance, and to fire’s emergence from wood, iron, or stone and its return to ash.
rows.anchor: ( ومنه معنى النجم النباتي الذي هو للشجر بمنزلة الفول للبشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn applies to all kinds of manifestation, not one particular object; together with kāf, the sign of creation, it causes things to appear.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذا الحرف اسما لما به ظهور أمر لم يختص بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn and kāf in God’s command to a thing, Be, and it is, express the appearance of all things through divine creative power.
rows.anchor: إنما قلنا لشيء إذا أردناه أن نقول له كن فيكون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets nūn as the inkpot from which the pen draws; this follows from the letter’s application to every manifestation.
rows.anchor: ولصدقه على كل مظهر فسره ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالدواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn appears in words for high land and emergence, such as najd and a young woman’s breast, sharing the sense of manifestation.
rows.anchor: وليلحظ موقعه في نجد فإنه اسم لما ارتفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other nūn words signify manifestation, including blowing, benefit, victory, piercing, digging, increase, and growth.
rows.anchor: وفي النفخ والنفع والنصر والنقر والنقب وما أشبهها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn is lofty, inward, and all-encompassing, supported by wāw and ending as it began; mīm is completed by a descending element and wāw’s alif supports its height.
rows.anchor: ولأجل علوه واستطبانه وأنه استغراق المظهر المبين كانت إقامته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn, mīm, and wāw signify two worlds: the first nūn is the light of sight and the closing nūn the light of the heart.
rows.anchor: وهذه الحروف الثلاثة ظاهرة في عالمين ظاهرهما المبدوء به وباطنهما المختوم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because nūn lies in the tens, it marks a hidden, lower doubling of hāʾ; it is visible beside hidden hāʾ and hidden beside manifest mīm, making the prior sura’s kingdom manifest.
rows.anchor: فكان ظاهرا بالإضافة إلى خفاء الهاء باطنا بالإضافة إلى ظهور الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every deed is completed through the light of knowledge, as outward signs depend on their hidden source; nūn is ink like the knowledge by which the pen reveals forms.
rows.anchor: ولذلك انبنى تمام كل عمل على نور علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the earth rests on a hidden cosmic fish called nūn, and people of Paradise first eat an extra portion of its liver together with the bull; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: ما بطن دون الأرض من النون الذي عليه الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden nūn beneath the earth contrasts with the visible emerald Mount Qāf encircling the world; scholars rule hearts through knowledge, while kings rule bodies through power.
rows.anchor: وقابل استبطان النون في الأرض ظهور القاف على ظاهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars and kings are the two groups that exercise authority over people, one through knowledge and the other through power.
rows.anchor: وهذان الصفنان من الخلق هما المستوليان على الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāf and nūn are paired in the openings of the suras and in Qurʾān and Furqān, linking visible power with the knowledge that discloses it.
rows.anchor: ولذلك أقيم المفصل من القرى بحرفي قاف ونون

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that people of Paradise first eat from the bull that grazed at the edges of Paradise; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: أول ما يطعمه أهل الجنة من الثور الذي عليه الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bull represents toil and labor on which earthly life rests; eating it in Paradise rewards people for worldly effort and releases them from the burden of earning.
rows.anchor: لأن صورة الثور هي معنى ما هو الكد والكدح وجهد العمل في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added liver portion represents the people’s share of foundational knowledge; their good original intention in religion is honored, and after eating both they enter repose.
rows.anchor: وأضيف لذلك زيادة كبد النون التي هي صورة حظهم نم أصل العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāf signifies strength, domination, and power; nūn makes that power intelligible through the light of knowledge.
rows.anchor: ما أتقنه بحكمته من ثناء المفصل القرآني على حرفي القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expansive Quranic portion serves learned people with rulings, stories, and difficult verses; short suras carry selected lessons suited to general listeners.
rows.anchor: ضمن ما عدا المفصل منه الذي هو من قاف إلى خاتمة الكتاب العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suras opened by encompassing, unseen letters have outward meanings for the wider community and inward meanings reserved for the Prophet’s family.
rows.anchor: والسور المفتتحة بالحروف العلية الإحاطة الغيبية المنحى المستندة إلى آحاد الأعداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mufassal repeats stories, admonitions, laws, reports, and judgment in many short suras so ordinary listeners can hear and absorb lessons from longer suras, including in obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: ذكر فيها من أطراف القصص والمواعظ والأحكام والأنباء وأمر الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāf fittingly opens the mufassal: its numerical progression from one to ten and a hundred signals encompassing scope, and its power imagery suits public governance.
rows.anchor: فكان أحق ما افتتح به مفصلهم حرف القاف الذي هو وتر الآحاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet often recited Sūrat Qāf in the Friday sermon, presenting the mufassal’s powerful opening to a general audience at communal prayer; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يكثر أن يقرأ في خطبة الجمعة سورة ( ق )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat Nūn pairs with Qāf by making its power manifest and adding knowledge that encompasses public affairs; power without knowledge can do more harm than good.
rows.anchor: وشفعت بسورة ( ن ) المظهرة ظاهر ( ق )

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: An unnamed early authority says authority unsupported by knowledge ends in humiliation; no grading applies.
rows.anchor: قال بعض السلف : كل عز لم يوطده علم فإلى ذل يؤول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The twenty-nine letter-opened suras encode nine ranks and a tenth that gathers and multiplies them, forming an encompassing structure throughout the Quran’s short suras.
rows.anchor: كان جميع السورة التسع والعشرين المفتتحة بالحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāf and nūn jointly contain the Quranic portion addressed especially to the public, through the visible mountain surrounding earth and the hidden fish beneath it.
rows.anchor: كذلك كان سورة ( ق ) وسورة ( ن ) قواما خاصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter-opened suras distinguish the Quran from earlier books by its comprehensive, final scope and the corresponding range of its contents.
rows.anchor: وبهذه السورة المفتتحة بالحروف ظهر اختصاص القرآن وتميز عن سائر الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All interpretations of the disconnected letters are valid within their encompassing implications, including divine, angelic, prophetic, created, oath, sura-opening, and numerical readings tied to outward or inward events.
rows.anchor: كل ما فسرت به من معنى يرجع إلى مقتضاها صحيحا في إحاطتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because these letters are independent and encompassing, they need no fixed syntactic place or case ending; any nominative, accusative, or genitive assignment is possible, unlike words whose meanings require grammatical relations.
rows.anchor: لا يختص بمحل مخصوص يلزمه علامة إعراب مخصوصة , فمهما قدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world’s order depends on sword and pen; nūn can mean sword, inkpot, or tablet, while the sword’s power suits Qāf and the pen’s knowledge suits this sura.
rows.anchor: ولما كان قوام هذا الوجود بالسيف والقلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author associates the sword with Qāf and al-Ḥadīd’s strength and power, following intervening admonition, threat, and reminders of blessings.
rows.anchor: وكان السيف قد تقدم في حيز القاف الذي افتتحت به سورة ( ق )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen is the first thing God created and commanded to write all events through Judgment Day, truly in the Preserved Tablet and figuratively on the pages of created things, thus displaying all knowledge.
rows.anchor: قلم القدرة الذي هو أول ما أبدعه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God then sealed the pen so it does not speak until Judgment Day; human writing comes from granted understanding, and the pen signifies decree and its detailed execution.
rows.anchor: ثم ختم على فيه فلم ينطق ولا ينطق إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may ascribe writing to the pen as a genus, personified because it performs the writers’ work, or may refer to writers by ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وجمعه وأجره مجرى أولي العلم للتعظيم لأنه فعل أفعالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If implied writers are intended, they may be angels writing in the clear record and Preserved Tablet, or every writer, including authors of Quraysh’s boycott document against Banū Hāshim and allies.
rows.anchor: إما الملائكة إن كان المراد ما كتب في الكتاب المبين واللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author recalls Quraysh’s pact to boycott Banū Hāshim and their allies until they surrendered the Prophet, as an example of a written deed.
rows.anchor: حتى أصحاب الصحيفة الظالمة التي تقاسموا فيها على أن يقاطعوا بني هاشم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whichever reading of the writers is taken, the oath concerns what is decreed, since nothing is written except what God determined.
rows.anchor: وكيف ما كان فهو إشارة إلى المقدر لأنه إنما يسطر ما قضى به وحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a lead-in to the denial of madness, the author recalls that the Prophet had lived among his audience for forty years, was their most virtuous and wise, and was known as the trustworthy one.
rows.anchor: قد عاشر المرسل إليهم دهرا طويلا وزمنا مديدا أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the great oath, God comforts the Prophet and refutes the accusation of madness, which arose only after the unmatched blessing bestowed on him.
rows.anchor: قال مجيبا هذا القسم العظيم رادا عليهم بأجلى ما يكون وأدله على المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing is God’s nurturing of the Prophet’s lofty aspirations and complete dispositions, and His choosing him for the Quran, which gathers all knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: أي بسبب إنعام { ربك } المربي لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensified denial honors the Prophet; the person who calls him mad deserves that name, and the accusation exceeds the earlier charge of misguidance.
rows.anchor: وأكد النفي زيادة في شرفه صل الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mulk had left open which of the Prophet and his opponents was plainly astray; evidence in its signs establishes their error and his guidance.
rows.anchor: فستعلمون من هو في ضلال مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial removes misery caused by defective reason and confirms happiness grounded in sound reason and God’s favor.
rows.anchor: فنفى عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم الشقاوة التي سببها فساد العقل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr says al-Mulk contains proofs so immense that minds cannot exhaust them, including reflection on the creation of the seven heavens; no grading applies.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما تضمنت سورة الملك من عظيم البراهين

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr glosses ṭibāqan as one layer matching another, deriving it from layering a sandal sole; he says this suggests equal dimensions and exact matching without excess or deficiency.
rows.anchor: أي يطابق بعضها بعضا من طابق النعل - إذا خصفها طبقا
